terms.gloss: define, say what a thing is
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.7: ante dēfīnīre, quid sit officium
terms.comment: With an object or an indirect question (quid sit). Lewis & Short: first “to set bounds to”, then “to define”, frequent in Cicero.

evidence: Quint. 12.1.1: quī ā M. Catōne fīnītur
Quint. 7.3.3 (Lewis & Short): ut sī fīniās equum
Cic. Off. 1.7: dēbet ā dēfīnītiōne proficīscī

phrases.latin: Placet igitur, quoniam omnis disputātiō dē officiō futūra est, ante dēfīnīre, quid sit officium
phrases.english: So, since this whole discussion is to be about duty, I think we should first define what duty is

phrases.latin: sit ergō nōbīs ōrātor, quem cōnstituimus, is, quī ā M. Catōne fīnītur, vir bonus dīcendī perītus
phrases.english: let the orator we are shaping, then, be the one Marcus Cato defined: a good man skilled in speaking

sources: Lewis & Short: definio · Lewis & Short: finio · Lewis & Short: definitio
